subject: ACME POC: Integration plan, success criteria, and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jared Cole <jared.cole@acme.com>

Subject: ACME POC: Integration plan, success criteria, and next steps

Hi Jared -

Great conversation earlier - thanks for walking through ACME's primary evaluation goals. Per our call, I put together a proposed POC plan + integration checklist attached (POC-MAP.pdf, integration-checklist.xlsx). High-level recap and asks below so we can lock timelines.

Recap / proposed POC structure
- Duration: 2 weeks (1 week integration + validation, 1 week evaluation + metrics)
- Scope: chat & retrieval-augmented generation for support triage; embeddings for semantic search; a small subset of tool calls for case lookups
- Success criteria (examples to confirm): p95 latency < 200ms for short responses, embeddings recall @ 10 > 0.75 on your benchmark, accurate tool calling for 90% of scripted flows

Immediate asks from ACME
1) Confirm success criteria (metrics + acceptance thresholds)
2) Provide a technical point-of-contact and service account details for test/dev environment
3) Confirm preferred start date (we suggested week of Jul 5)

Integration notes for your engineers (details in attachment):
- SDK: official Redwood Node + Python SDKs supported (quickstart link in doc)
- API routes: /v1/generate (chat/generation), /v1/embeddings, /v1/call-tool for tool calling
- Streaming: SSE or chunked HTTP streaming supported (we'll provide sample code)
- Auth: API keys for POC; dedicated key scoped to ACME POC project

Next steps
- Jared: confirm criteria + tech lead (Samir?) by EOD Wed Jun 30
- Rafael: coordinate kickoff + send initial integration stubs
- Marissa: schedule kickoff and handle commercial/Docusign paperwork

Thanks - I attached the POC-MAP and integration checklist for your team to review.

--Marissa

Subject: Re: ACME POC: Integration plan, success criteria, and next steps

Marissa -

Thanks for the recap and the materials. Confirming ACME is aligned on a 2-week POC starting Jul 5. Samir (cc'd) will be the technical lead for the integration. I've attached our internal POC requirements doc for reference (acme-poc-requirements.docx).

ACME success criteria (initial):
- Latency: p95 < 200ms for 64-token responses for top-tier routes
- Throughput: support 50 concurrent sessions during peak test window
- Quality: embeddings recall @10 >= 0.78 on our sample set; generation F1 on canned prompts >= 0.82
- Tooling: tool-calls correctly routed for >= 90% of scripted flows (case lookup, SLA check)

Timeline we propose:
- Week 1 (Jul 5-9): integration + smoke tests; Redwood provides SDK examples + streaming samples; ACME provides service account and staging dataset
- Week 2 (Jul 12-16): evaluation runs, metrics collection, and a wrap-up demo/decision meeting on Fri Jul 16

Samir, can you confirm you can take the kickoff this week and share credentials for staging?

-Jared

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 15:47:00 -0400
Subject: Re: ACME POC: Integration plan, success criteria, and next steps

Hi Samir / Jared -

Thanks - happy to own the technical integration. Quick implementation plan and what we'll supply for the POC.

Integration plan (week 1)
1) Kickoff & environment setup (1 day)
   - Exchange staging API key (scoped) or service account for ACME test org
   - Confirm endpoint / routing for dev vs. prod
2) SDK & quickstart (1 day)
   - We'll provide Node + Python snippets that cover: auth, chat streaming, embeddings calls, and tool-calling flow
3) Streaming & tool calling (2 days)
   - Streaming: SSE endpoint with chunked tokens; example using EventSource in Node and requests with chunked transfer in Python
   - Tool calling: define tool schemas; Redwood will accept a JSON tool declaration and invoke a callback to your tool endpoint (/acme/tool/call). We'll provide a local stub for offline testing
4) Load smoke tests + metrics capture (1-2 days)

API notes / examples
- Chat generation (non-streaming): POST https://inference.redwood.com/v1/generate
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <POC_KEY>
Body: {"model":"redwood-1.1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"..."}],"max_tokens":256}
- Streaming (SSE): GET https://inference.redwood.com/v1/generate/stream
Query: ?model=redwood-1.1&project=acme-poc- Example Node streaming (pseudo):
  const es = new EventSource(streamUrl, {headers:{Authorization:`Bearer ${KEY}`}})
  es.onmessage = (e) => { /* handle token chunks */ }
- Embeddings: POST https://inference.redwood.com/v1/embeddings
Body: {"model":"redwood-embed-1.0","input":["...","..."]}
- Tool calling: POST https://inference.redwood.com/v1/call-tool
Body: {"tool_id":"case_lookup","input":{...}}

Security & limits
- Scoped API key for POC (will expire after 30 days)
- Rate limit for POC key: 120 reqs/min by default; we can raise to 300 reqs/min during smoke test window if needed
- Data handling: logs for POC will be retained 30 days; full retention policy available if you need SOC2 artifacts

Deliverables from Redwood
- SDK snippets + streaming examples (repo link)
- Integration stub (integration-stub.md) for tool callbacks
- Basic dashboard instrumentation for p95 latency + embedding recall

Samir - can you share a staging endpoint and a contact for your infra team? Also let us know if you prefer API key or short-lived service account tokens.

Thanks,
Rafael
Staff Engineer, Integrations | Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.com

Attachment: integration-stub.md
